summary:
Moon Cadet is a browser-based, first-person 3D simulation where the player works as a lunar outpost engineer. We built four hands-on missions:
1. Powering a habitat with solar arrays, batteries and a converter
2. Setting up life support with water loops, electrolysis, CO₂ scrubbing and a Sabatier reactor 
3. Running a hydroponic greenhouse
4. Responding to a radiation emergency by driving a rover to seal the shelter within ten minutes

The game addresses the challenge by turning real Moon-base engineering into something people can practise instead of just read about. Players see how power, air, water, food and radiation safety depend on one another, and they learn to troubleshoot under pressure.

It matters because a lasting human presence on the Moon needs engineers who think in whole systems. Moon Cadet makes that thinking accessible, engaging and free, and it can inspire students who may one day help build the next Moon base.
details:
Moon Cadet is a first-person 3D simulation that runs in the browser. The player walks around a lunar site, picks up equipment, connects cables, pipes and ducts, and operates consoles, using the keyboard and mouse. There are four missions:

Power generation: Survey sites, then install solar panels, batteries, a converter and a distribution unit.

Life support: Set up water purification, electrolysis, a CO₂ scrubber, a Sabatier reactor and fans.

Farm maintenance: Refill water, dose nutrients, inspect plants, check the LEDs, harvest and replant.

Radiation emergency: Find the breach with a detector, suit up, drive the rover for regolith and seal the shelter within a 10-minute timer.

The game has different playable components like picking up and placing objects, connecting equipment, etc. It helps the player understand life requirements on the moon.

Benefits of Moon Cadet:

It is free and needs no installation or account.

Players learn by doing, with instant feedback, instead of reading about it.

It shows how power, air, water, food and shelter depend on each other.

We want to make space engineering approachable for students and curious players. We want them to see the Moon as a place that needs systems thinkers, and to feel inspired to pursue STEM and space careers.

Tools and technology used:

Languages and rendering: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3 and Three.js (r128, WebGL).

Browser features: The Web Audio API for sound, the Pointer Lock API for mouse look, and localStorage for saved records.

Fonts: Rajdhani and IBM Plex Mono from Google Fonts.

Hardware: A computer with a keyboard and mouse.

How our project is creative:

The player is the engineer who does the work, not a viewer watching a diagram.

Each mission plays differently: wiring, plumbing, farming and rover driving under time pressure.

The cockpit-style HUD gives a convincing mission-control feel.

Factors we considered:

Realism: One-sixth gravity is shown when the player jumps, a closed water and oxygen loop, a safe nutrient range and a crew radiation dose limit (50 mSv).

Learning: Guided task lists, hints and on-screen messages when something is wrong; intended to make learning easy for the player.

Accessibility: A drag-to-look fallback if the mouse can’t be captured, and reduced-motion support.

Limits: It works best on desktop, not touch screens.
